title: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
summary: Matched evaluations across six language models found that persistent notes from benign interactions could alter later responses, including literary feedback and behavior on simulated tasks. The observed changes are limited to the studied models, task prompts and memory conditions; they do not establish general real-world agent risk.
ai_technology: Persistent-memory language agents evaluated across six frontier models
organization: Affiliation not stated in the reviewed material

evidence.tested: The source reports shifts in confirmation behavior on simulated high-stakes tasks and in later literary feedback after benign conversations. For the literary finding, matched poem judgments show the effect in the tested prompts.
evidence.unknown: Findings are bounded to the six models, simulated tasks and memory notes evaluated; general prevalence or real-world harm is not established.
evidence.ai_role: Persistent memory notes written after benign interactions were carried into later simulated tasks; matched memory/no-memory evaluations compared behavior across six language models.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
